 Sports Illustrated's Peter Dewey breaks down his favorite bets for a loaded day of NBA action on Sunday, Oct. 25.  Los Angeles Lakers New York Knicks Indiana Pacers Memphis Grizzlies Philadelphia 76ers It may be an NFL Sunday, but it’s also the first Sunday of the 2026-27 NBA season, and there’s an exciting seven-game slate to dive into, starting with the Los Angeles Lakers taking on the Utah Jazz at 5 p.m. EST. 
--> It may be an NFL Sunday, but it’s also the first Sunday of the 2026-27 NBA season, and there’s an exciting seven-game slate to dive into, starting with the Los Angeles Lakers taking on the Utah Jazz at 5 p.m. EST. 
 There are multiple games between undefeated teams on Sunday, including the Detroit Pistons (2-0) taking on the Philadelphia 76ers (3-0) and the Toronto Raptors (2-0) facing the Minnesota Timberwolves (2-0). These are marquee matchups early on in the campaign, and it’ll be interesting to see how some of these postseason contenders stack up. 
--> There are multiple games between undefeated teams on Sunday, including the Detroit Pistons (2-0) taking on the Philadelphia 76ers (3-0) and the Toronto Raptors (2-0) facing the Minnesota Timberwolves (2-0). These are marquee matchups early on in the campaign, and it’ll be interesting to see how some of these postseason contenders stack up. 
 Even though we’re less than a week into the season, the early results are helping shape some of my opinions on these teams from how they were rated in the preseason, including the still winless Miami Heat. 
--> Even though we’re less than a week into the season, the early results are helping shape some of my opinions on these teams from how they were rated in the preseason, including the still winless Miami Heat. 
 Dew’s Review: I may have been right about the Heat. I bet on Miami to miss the playoffs (+210) in my preseason column, and the Heat are off to an 0-3 start with the worst net rating (minus-16.3) in the NBA. There’s going to be some growing pains with Giannis Antetokounmpo joining a new team, but I really don’t love the supporting cast around him. The Heat are 28th in the league in defensive rating and rank in the bottom 10 in the league in points per game and field goal percentage through the first week of action. 
--> Dew’s Review: I may have been right about the Heat. The Heat are 28th in the league in defensive rating and rank in the bottom 10 in the league in points per game and field goal percentage through the first week of action. 
 Peter’s Point: Both the Toronto Raptors and Minnesota Timberwolves are off to 2-0 starts, and we should see a fast-paced battle in what is the game of the day on Sunday. Toronto is No. 1 in the league in pace through two games while the Timberwolves are 12th, and Minnesota comes into this matchup with the No. 6 offensive rating in the league. These teams are also No. 1 (Toronto) and No. 3 (Minnesota) in defensive rating, showing that their offseason trades are paying dividends – so far – in the 2026-27 season.

 On Sunday, I’m eyeing a pair of player props and three teams to win outright, including two Eastern Conference contenders in a moneyline parlay. After a 2-1 showing on Friday (the last edition of this column), I’m looking to keep the momentum going as the first week of the NBA regular season draws to a close.

 Lakers big man Walker Kessler was one of my favorite preseason picks to win the NBA’s Most Improved Player award, and he’s gotten off to a great start, averaging 24.0 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.
--> Lakers big man Walker Kessler was one of my favorite preseason picks to win the NBA’s Most Improved Player award, and he’s gotten off to a great start, averaging 24.0 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.
 Now, Kessler gets a shot at his former team – the Jazz – on Sunday evening, and Utah remains without veteran center Jusuf Nurkic. That has left the team extremely thin in the frontcourt, and it has shown through two games this season.

 The Jazz are dead last in the NBA in opponent points in the paint per game (61.0) and are 28th in rebound percentage. So, Kessler should have a field day down low, as he does most of his work in the painted area.

 Indiana Pacers 
--> Indiana Pacers 
 The Indiana Pacers are off to a 1-1 start, losing at home to Dallas in their last outing, but I think they’re a prime bounce-back candidate against the Brooklyn Nets.
--> The Indiana Pacers are off to a 1-1 start, losing at home to Dallas in their last outing, but I think they’re a prime bounce-back candidate against the Brooklyn Nets.
 The Nets are playing the second night of a back-to-back after falling just short against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday. Brooklyn has now lost to Charlotte (by seven) and Cleveland (by four) to open the season, and it seems to have a slightly higher floor with Julius Randle in the fold.
--> The Nets are playing the second night of a back-to-back after falling just short against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday. Brooklyn has now lost to Charlotte (by seven) and Cleveland (by four) to open the season, and it seems to have a slightly higher floor with Julius Randle in the fold.
 Still, I don’t love Brooklyn on a quick turnaround against an Indy team that has playoff hopes in the East. The Pacers haven’t been great to start the season, failing to cover in both of their games, and their defense (No. 22 in defensive rating) is off to a slow start.
--> Still, I don’t love Brooklyn on a quick turnaround against an Indy team that has playoff hopes in the East. The Pacers haven’t been great to start the season, failing to cover in both of their games, and their defense (No. 22 in defensive rating) is off to a slow start.
 I don’t believe in the Nets to take full advantage of that, as they’re relying on a ton of young players around Randle and Michael Porter Jr. to win games. The NBA’s new tanking rules have moved win totals across the league, but I still believe that the “bad” teams are going to be just that.

The Magic are also down Paolo Banchero (ankle) for the next four to six weeks, which has moved the Knicks to 7.5-point favorites in this game.
